about: What NuclearLang, Dragonfly and their tools can do today, by area. Each row names the kinds and commands that do it.

rows.title: Can: an HTTP API with validation (backend)
rows.summary: A backend exposes REST routes with controllers (`@get`, `@post`, `@put`, `@patch`, `@delete`), reads and answers validated models, turns a `Result` error into its HTTP status and publishes its contract and OpenAPI document.
body: - `@controller("books") controller BooksController(books: BooksAppComponent)` with one method per route; `{id}` in a route is a path parameter, a model parameter is the JSON body.
- Models validate the input with rule decorators (`@required`, `@minLength`, `@maxLength`, `@min`, `@max`, `@pattern`, `@email`, `@url`); an invalid body is a 422.
- An `Err(NotFound(...))` answers 404; `Invalid` 400, `Unauthorized` 401, `Forbidden` 403, `Conflict` 409. A `@post` answers 201; `status = 200` in the decorator changes it.
- The build serves `/.nuclear/contract.json` and `/.nuclear/openapi.json`.
- The same Nuclear builds as a Python service (`fastapi`) or a TypeScript one (`nestjs`).

rows.title: Can: a database with entities, relations, queries, transactions and migrations (backend)
rows.summary: A backend stores data with entities (tables), repositories (CRUD and queries built line by line), relations between entities, pages, transactions and migrations, on SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL or MariaDB.
body: - `entity` with `@primary(generated = true)`, `@column(length, unique, index, nullable, default, name)`, `@created`, `@updated`.
- Relations: `@manyToOne` (with its column `<name>Id`), `@oneToMany`, `@manyToMany` + `@joinTable`, `@oneToOne` + `@joinColumn`; loaded with `relations("tasks")`.

- `repository`: `find`, `findAll`, `save`, `remove` come with it; a method's lines build one query: `where({...})` with `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `ne`, `like`, `ilike`, `oneOf`, `isNull`, `between`; `orderBy`, `limit`, `offset`; then `getOne()`, `getMany()`, `paginate(page, size)`, `count()`, `exists()`, `update({...})`, `delete()`.
- `@transactional` on a use case's `exec`: one transaction; an `Err` rolls it back.
- Migrations: `dragonfly migrate make "<message>"`, `dragonfly migrate`, `dragonfly migrate down`.
- Plugins: `sqlite`, `postgres`, `mysql`, `mariadb`. Tests run on an in-memory database.
Checked on SQLite; the other databases were not run against a real server yet.

rows.title: Can: call another HTTP API (every platform)
rows.summary: A repository whose methods carry `@get`, `@post`, `@put`, `@patch` or `@delete` and no body calls the `Http(baseUrl)` connection: path parameters, the query or the body are filled from the method's parameters, and an error status is the `Err` of its `Result`.
body: ```nuclear
@repository(path = "character")
repository CharacterRepository
@get(path = ":id")
one(id: int) Result<Error, Character>
- `:id` takes the parameter `id`; the other parameters go to the query (GET) or the body.
- The connection is `Http(baseUrl = "https://...")` in `appConfig`.
- A JSON key that is not the field's name gets `@key("air_date")` on the model's field.
- On mobile and web, `cache`, `ttl` and `retry` are options of the request; on mobile, `saveLocal = true` keeps the answers in the device's database.
- `dragonfly gen resource ... --from-json <url>` writes the whole resource from the API's own answer.

rows.title: Can: events, a cache and AI agents (backend)
rows.summary: A backend publishes and consumes events (in the process or through Kafka), caches with Redis, and declares AI agents: tools, agents with memory per thread and graphs of steps, on Ollama or OpenAI models, with a vector store.
body: - Events: `~publish("topic", value)`; `listener Name` with `@consumer("topic")` methods. Plugins `events` and `kafka`.
- Cache: the `redis` plugin.

- AI (plugin `ai`, with `ollama` or `openai`): `tools Name` (each method with a doc comment is a tool), `agent Name(tools: T)` with a `prompt`, `@state(S) graph Name` whose methods are nodes (`@start`, `@next("node")`), a `state` for the graph, `Chroma` vectors (plugin `chroma`).
- A test replaces the model with `FakeModel(["answer"])`.
The Nuclear Developer itself is written with these kinds.

rows.title: Can: a mobile app (mobile)
rows.summary: A mobile app with screens and navigation, state managers, forms with validation, translations, a session with roles and guards, events, HTTP repositories with cache, an encrypted local database, and AI chats and flows; it runs on Android, iOS, desktop and web.
body: - Views: `stateless` and `stateful` with the UI toolkit's classes; `@screen(route, providers, acl, transition)`; navigation by screen (`context.goTo`, `pushTo`, `goBack`).
- State: `statemanager` + state model, `<State>Builder` in the view.
- Forms: a form model with rules, a `formmanager`, `DragonflyForm` in the view.
- Texts: `"component.screen.key".tr()` from `assets/i18n/<locale>/<component>.json`.
- Session and access: `SessionManager`, `guard`, `@acl(roles = [...])`, `@screen(acl = {...})`.
- Events: `event`, `Events.publish`, `@on(Event)`.
- Data: HTTP repositories (`cache`, `ttl`, `retry`), and a local database: `@primary` on a model gives it an encrypted table, `saveLocal = true` keeps what a GET answers.
- AI (plugin `genkit`): `tools`, `chat`, `flow`, `remote`, `knowledge`.
- Tests: `@mock`, `@test`, `@states`, `@widget`, integration tests.
- Run and debug: `dragonfly run`, `dragonfly device` (a test device in its own window), breakpoints on `.nuc` lines in VS Code.

rows.title: Can: a web app (web)
rows.summary: A web app with screens and routing, views as HTML functions, state managers, HTTP repositories, use cases, events, guards and tests. The words are the mobile platform's; it is the first version of the platform.
body: - Views: `stateless` and `stateful` with `build() Element` and HTML functions (`main`, `ul`, `li`, `button`) with named attributes and `children`. No JSX.
- `@screen(route, providers, acl, notFound)`; navigation by screen: `goTo(Screen, id = 7)`, `goBack()`.
- `statemanager` + state model, `<State>Builder` with one callback per state.
- `repository` over HTTP (`cache`, `ttl`, `retry`), `usecase`, `appcomponent`, `service`, `event`, `guard`.
- Tests: `@mock`, `@test`, `@states`, `@widget` with `renderScreen`.
- `dragonfly new <name> -p web`, `dragonfly build | install | run | test`.
The NuclearLang website is written with it.

rows.title: Can: generate the finished code of a resource from its data
rows.summary: `dragonfly gen resource` writes, on any platform, the models, the repository, a use case per action, the facade, the controller or the screen and the tests of a resource, all compiling; the fields come from a list, from an example answer of an API (a file or a URL) or from a spec.
body: - `--fields "id:int name:string origin:Origin?"`, `--from-json <file|url>` (nested objects become models, a list under `results` a page, `null` an optional field) or `--from-spec <spec.md>` (its example answer, its `Key | Type` table, its `GET <url>` line).
- `--source rest[:<base url>]` (an API) or `--source db` (an entity and its queries, backend only).
- `--actions list,get,search,create,update,delete`; `--screen <screen>` on mobile and web; `--dry-run` shows the files.
- It refuses, before writing, a field type nobody declared, a name another file declares and a source the platform has no pieces for. Nothing is overwritten.

- `dragonfly gen usecase <component> <Name>` wires a use case the project declares: its alias in the facade and, on the backend, `--route "POST orders/{id}/cancel"` adds its route to the controller of `orders` (made when missing). With `--calls <Repository>.<method>` it also writes the use case, when all it does is call that method.
- `dragonfly make <kind> <component> <Name>` writes the smallest file of any kind of the platform.
- The same generators are MCP tools and the first stage of the Loop.

rows.title: Can: build the same project with another dialect of its platform
rows.summary: A backend written once builds as FastAPI (Python) or as NestJS (TypeScript): change `dialect` in `config.nuc` and build. No other file changes, because kinds, decorators, the library and the tests belong to the platform.
body: ```nuclear
dragonfly(platform = "backend", dialect = "nestjs")   // was "fastapi"
Then `dragonfly build && dragonfly install && dragonfly test`. The example `tasks_api` is built and tested with both.
The exception: code that uses a library of one target through its type definitions is tied to that target's dialect. Mobile and web have one dialect each today.

rows.title: Can: generate an app's models and repositories from its backend
rows.summary: An app that declares a backend's contract in `config.nuc` gets its models and one typed repository per controller generated at build time; a change in the backend that breaks the app is a compile error in the app.
body: `contracts(tasks_api = "../tasks_api")` or a URL; `nuclear contracts update`, `nuclear contracts list`. The generated files are in `contracts/<name>/`. Works for mobile and web apps over a backend of any dialect.

rows.title: Can: check a project, apply the exact fixes and format it
rows.summary: `nuclear check` reports every error of a file or a project with its code, place and fix (JSON for agents); `nuclear fix` applies the exact fixes; `nuclear fmt` rewrites the layout; `dragonfly explain` tells a run-time error or a failing test at its `.nuc` lines.
body: - `nuclear check . --json`: syntax, names, results, the library, the kinds' rules and the project's architecture, all at once. It also writes the project map (`.nuclear/map.md`).
- `nuclear fix <folder|file>`: applies every exact fix, then reports what is left.
- `nuclear fmt <file|folder> [--check]`: spacing, indentation and blank lines; it never reorders.
- `dragonfly explain`: reads a stack or a test's output and answers the message, a hint and the `.nuc` lines.
- `dragonfly repair` (mobile): rebuilds from scratch until the target's analyzer finds no errors.
- `dragonfly doctor`: what the machine lacks.

rows.title: Can: take a spec to tested code with AI agents, on your machine or under a frontier model
rows.summary: The Loop runs a spec through generate, plan, tests first, code, verification, security, artifacts and deploy with the local agents; any MCP client (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) can lead it; every run is documented, retried from where it failed and exportable as CI.
body: - Local only: `nuclear-loop run specs/<id>/spec.md --lead local`, or `/task` in the chat.
- Under a lead: `--lead claude`, or the MCP tools `developer_task`, `developer_retry`, `developer_review`.
- Specs imported from Jira or a GitHub issue (VS Code).
- The internet for facts: `web_search`, `web_read`, `api_inspect` (MCP tools).
- CI: `nuclear-loop export github|gitlab|bitbucket`; `nuclear-loop ci` runs the same commands locally.
- A chat about the project with the local assistant (VS Code).

rows.title: Can: add your own kinds, definitions and dialects without touching the compiler
rows.summary: A project or the community adds a kind as a package (`kinds/<name>/` with TOML, templates and a runtime), brings type definitions of a library in `<project>/defs/`, and a new target is a new dialect: all data, never Rust.
body: - `nuclear kind new <name> -p <platform> -d <dialect>` writes a kind package's skeleton; `dragonfly add <folder>` installs it. A package implemented for some dialects ties the project to them (`N0306`).
- `dragonfly flutter add <package>` adds a package to a mobile app and generates its type definitions.
- `nuclear dialect check <name|path>` validates a dialect's files.
